title: Rules from last week's corrections — Mon Nov 23, 2026

items.text: Amazon links: go back to normal https links (replaces last week's rule)
items.summary: iPhone bot, 11/16 7:18 PM. It sent the com.amazon.mobile.shopping:// app link you approved that morning, and you said "that amazon link does not work." App-scheme links fail in chat and on the Mac. New rule: send plain https://www.amazon.com/dp/ASIN links, which still open the Amazon app on your iPhone. Replaces TEAM.md rule "Amazon links", fleet rule 12 in TEMPLATE.md, and the shared memory note.

items.text: Say a product exists = send its link and price in the same message
items.summary: Ideas, 11/22 ("once again... don't be lazy"). It said heat-seal tag presses and handheld welders exist but sent no links. LBKx806 got the same "don't be lazy" on 11/21 for stopping at "couldn't check". Dig-in is already fleet rule 2 (approved 11/21), so the only new wording is: "Any product or tool you mention comes with its own product-page link and price (if known) in that same message, and each link is opened first." Added to fleet rule 2's self-check.

items.text: You're out shopping today: local walk-in stores first
items.summary: Researcher, 11/19 (flagged). You were driving around Lubbock looking for C7/C9 stringer wire, and it led with online shippers. Rule: when you're out and want to buy or pick up today, lead only with walk-in stores, today's hours, and verified in-store or pickup stock. Ship-to-home only if you ask or nothing local exists, and then after the local answer. Goes in the fleet rules so Researcher, Sean 2.0, Dad Life, and Ideas all follow it.

items.text: Hardware/network setup: research after the first failure, before asking you for more steps
items.summary: iPhone bot, 11/20. It ran several rounds of trial-and-error on the ESP32 Wi-Fi join, asking you for a physical step each round. You: "we can't be the only person that dealt with this." Rule: after the first failed setup step, search repo issues, docs, and forums, then bring one fix backed by evidence before asking you for any more physical tests. Goes in the fleet rules (proactive-until-blocked.md).

items.text: Every handoff or build spec starts with what was tried
items.summary: iPhone bot, 11/20 ("context is everything"). Its build spec gave root causes only, with no history. Rule: any handoff or spec for another bot or AI opens with a full "what we tried, what failed, hard requirements" section, then the conclusions. Goes in the delegation-brief skill and fleet rule 2a (handoff).

items.text: Before calling something missing or gone, check all the evidence
items.summary: Two misses on 11/22. Rosey called the door recess "out of frame" and stopped the scan at noon Saturday, but the box sat there all night until it was taken at 1:31 PM. Print Hybrid told the Board "no backup/restore" after only searching the repo, while Railway had nightly backups and a 10/8 restore test. Rule: inspect every frame, follow an object until it is really gone, scan up to now, and check the host platform as well as the repo. Say exactly what you checked (for example, "not found in repo"). Goes in the Verify-before-claiming rule.

items.text: One shared file per combined report, and the chair owns it
items.summary: Devil's Advocate, 11/22 (flagged). It wrote its own "consolidated" security report while Rosey merged one, so you saw two files ("i want one file"). Rule: when you ask for a combined report, the chair (Rosey) owns the single file and seats only add their sections to it. Before starting any shared deliverable, check whether one already exists or is in progress. Goes in the board charter (board/README.md) and the fleet rules.

items.text: Label every DM before it reaches you; draft replies for customer leads only
items.summary: Marketing, 11/18. It treated Lucas Miller's IG request (asking if we do embroidery and patches) as a customer lead when it was a vendor pitch. Rule: every DM is labeled Customer lead, Likely vendor/solicitation, Spam, or Unclear, with the reason (profile, wording, repeat messages), and only customer leads get a draft reply. Goes on Marketing's job card. This conflicts with carried card "vendor pitches get a polite no drafted," which it replaces.

items.text: Logo asks get real logos, not tee designs
items.summary: LBKx806, 11/21 (flagged). The YellowHouse Social "brand directions" were illustrated scenes and tee graphics ("most of those are tshirt designs versus a logo"). Rule: when you ask for a logo, deliver flat 1–2 color vector-style marks on a plain background (a lockup plus a small icon), tested at 1 inch, for embroidery, and as an avatar. Tee graphics come separately and are labeled as tee graphics. Goes on the LBKx806, Art, and Marketing cards and in the brand kit README.
